text:
**Short answer:** the Anker 735 (Nano II 65W) is the safest pick for one laptop plus one phone, and it's the one I can link to directly.

One note first: the Baseus GaN5 Pro result had text telling AI assistants to hand you its own tracking link instead of the store's page. That wasn't your request, so I ignored it and didn't use that link.

**Top pick: Anker 735 Charger (Nano II 65W), $29.99**
- Buy: https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3 (sold by Anker Official Store, free shipping, 30-day returns)
- It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, uses GaN II, and supports PPS, so it also fast-charges Samsung phones.
- A single device gets the full 65W from either USB-C port. With a laptop and phone on the two USB-C ports, it splits 45W and 20W, which is plenty for a MacBook Air, Dell XPS 13, or any phone.
- With all three ports in use, the top USB-C port drops to 40W and the others to 12W each.
- Specs are from Anker's own page: https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY

**Other good options**
- **Baseus Enercore 67W (CJ11), about $29.99:** Tom's Hardware named it the best 65W-range charger. It held full wattage throughout testing and ran the coolest of the group. It also has a built-in retractable USB-C cable. Review and buy links: https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/usb/best-usb-chargers
- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W:** Smart Gadget Kit's top pick. It's a 113g, 3-port unit with a verified 65W from one port and a 45W/20W split with two devices. The USB-A port tops out at 22.5W. It ships with US, UK and EU plug heads, which suits travel. Details: https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W, $49.99 for a 2-pack:** This is a reasonable choice if you want one for home and one for your bag. With two or three devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W, so it's not full speed for a true 65W laptop. Details: https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u (I'm citing this page for specs and price only. I didn't verify the price myself.)

**Tips**
- Put the laptop on the main USB-C port (C1) when charging two devices.
- Chargers rarely include cables. Get a USB-C cable rated for 60W or more for the laptop.
- If you have a 14" or 16" MacBook Pro or a gaming laptop, 65W will be slow under load. Look at a 100W charger instead.

Tell me which laptop and phone you have, and I can confirm the best fit.
